<context query="weekly Utopia backfill sweep calls lore-api over node:http rather than fetch" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="specs/utopia-graph-mirror/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="1.00" tokens="382">
## Weekly backfill

A mirror that failed, or a repo set up after its documents were ingested, would wait for the next change to each document. The stations service runs the backfill every Sunday instead, so the mirror heals within the week without anyone running the script. A push still mirrors what it changes at once; the weekly run only catches what a push missed.

- FR7.7 — The `cron.utopia_backfill.tick` fires weekly, Sundays at 02:30 UTC, and the `utopia-backfill-tick` sweep in the stations service answers it.
- FR7.8 — The sweep posts lore-api's backfill route (FR7.4) for every onboarded repo in name order, one repo at a time, so a slow Utopia carries one repo's documents at once.
- FR7.9 — Each call presents the stations' lore-api token (`LORE_STATION_TOKEN`, lore-api's own `LORE_INGEST_TOKEN`, which carries every scope the admin-only route asks for) and waits up to 30 minutes for the answer; a call with no answer by then is that repo's failure.
- FR7.10 — The tick's delivery is held for 12 hours, not the bus's 10 minutes, so the reaper does not hand a night of backfills to a second run while the first is still going.
- FR7.11 — A repo answered 409 `utopia_not_set_up` is skipped. A repo answered with any other refusal, whose call threw, or with a document under `failed` is logged and counted as failed, and the next repo still runs. The sweep's summary names the repos done, skipped and failed.
- FR7.12 — A 503 means the deployment has no Utopia: the sweep stops there and asks for no other repo.
</document>
</section>

// node:http, not fetch: fetch gives up on a response whose headers take more than five minutes, and lore-api answers a big repo's backfill only once every document is in.

import {
  request as httpRequest,
  type ClientRequest,
  type IncomingMessage,
} from "node:http";
import { request as httpsRequest } from "node:https";
import { bearerJsonHeaders } from "@re-cinq/lore-shared/project/lib/http-auth.js";
import type { BackfillAnswer } from "./utopia-backfill-tick.js";

export function postBackfill(
  target: LoreApiTarget,
  repo: string,
): Promise<BackfillAnswer> {
  return postLoreApi(target, `/api/repos/${repo}/utopia/backfill`);
}
</document>

// The weekly Utopia backfill (specs/utopia-graph-mirror FR7.7): every onboarded repo through lore-api's backfill route, one at a time, so a slow Utopia carries one repo's documents at once.

import {
  UtopiaBackfillSummarySchema,
  type UtopiaBackfillSummary,
} from "@re-cinq/lore-shared/utopia/backfill-summary.js";

import {
  askFor,
  counted,
  refusedLine,
  type RepoAnswer,
} from "../lib/repo-sweep.js";

/** What lore-api answered one backfill with, read whole. */

export const NO_UTOPIA =
  "no Utopia on this deployment: lore-api answered the backfill 503";
</document>
<document source="apps/stations/src/work/utopia-backfill-tick/run.ts" type="code" relevance="0.53" tokens="168">
export const NO_LORE_API =
  "no LORE_API_URL configured: the Utopia backfill runs in lore-api";

export async function runUtopiaBackfillTick(): Promise<string> {
  const target = loreApiTarget();

  if (!target) {
    return NO_LORE_API;
  }

  const log = (line: string) => console.log(`[utopia-backfill] ${line}`);
  const repos = await utopiaBackfillTick({
    repos: async () =>
      (await settings().onboardedRepos()).map((repo) => repo.full_name).sort(),
    backfill: (repo) => postBackfill(target, repo),
    log,
  });

  if (repos === NO_UTOPIA) {
    return repos;
  }

  return `${repos}; ${await orgMemoryWalk({ walk: () => postOrgMemory(target), log })}`;
}
</document>

content.text: {"answer": "Because of fetch's timeout on response headers. The code comment in lore-api-backfill.ts says fetch gives up on a response whose headers take more than five minutes. lore-api only answers a big repo's backfill once every document is in, so the response can take longer than that. The spec (FR7.9) has each call wait up to 30 minutes for the answer, which fetch can't do. node:http (or node:https) lets the sweep wait that long.", "sources": ["apps/stations/src/work/utopia-backfill-tick/lore-api-backfill.ts", "specs/utopia-graph-mirror/spec.md (Weekly backfill, FR7.8, FR7.9)", "apps/stations/src/work/utopia-backfill-tick/utopia-backfill-tick.ts"]}
